content_of_post_to_comment: In the Royal Navy there was a saying, “Cordite is safe so long as you remember it's dangerous.” There is an eternal cycle of danger. A dangerous thing is guarded against and it stops killing. People forget that it is dangerous and it starts killing again.
comment: The tricky part is that successful safeguards make themselves seem unnecessary. Perhaps the real test of a safety culture is whether it can preserve a sense of danger even when nothing bad has happened for decades.
